title: BE VERY CAREFUL — READ THE FINE PRINT
body:
I purchased a personalised journal from LastingChange for $131, believing I was making a one-off purchase.

What was not made clear to me during the purchase process was that I was apparently also signing up for an ongoing monthly subscription.

The recurring subscription was hidden in the small print rather than being clearly and prominently disclosed.

I certainly did not knowingly agree to a monthly subscription, and I am extremely disappointed that a company selling a product centred around personal wellbeing chooses to use this sort of subscription model.

Whether the terms technically contain the information somewhere in the fine print is beside the point for me. Customers should not have to hunt through small print to discover that a $131 purchase has turned into an ongoing financial commitment of $55 per month.

My advice to anyone considering purchasing: read absolutely everything before entering your payment details and check your account afterwards for recurring charges.

For me, this has completely undermined my trust in the company and turned what should have been a positive purchase into a very sour experience.

author: Nicbrac

title: TOTAL SCAM!
body:
Much like the other reviewers here, I would strongly caution not to engage with this company as it is a blatant scam. You will be charged for an ongoing subscription to an app that offers no value whatsoever.

You will not be able to manage your subscription nor cancel it via your App Store account, their website or from within the app itself. They will continue to charge you even after deleting your account and deleting the app. This behavior should be illegal. 

Don’t engage!! You will lose money.
author: Johavoc

title: Purposeful Money Grab
body:
Do not support this company. If you choose to purchase only the book, you will be charged for the app as well. You will then be refused a refund. The responses on each of these reviews from the company is a facade, and for public appeal only. Once the company contacts or responds to you regarding a refund for wrongful charging of customer dollars, they cite that digital product refunds are not applicable. 

In short, this company’s business model is built upon wrongfully charging customers, and paying influencers to push their product. 

The product itself is underwhelming. Many comparative apps and books can be found for free or within $5. 

I have been in continuous contact with the company - I do not require a response asking me to contact you, but I have no doubt you will paste it below to seem as though you care for your customer’s opinions.

author: Kerrilili

title: Falls short of expectations
body:
After purchasing and using The Lasting Change app, I’m compelled to share my experience to help others make an informed decision.

The app significantly underdelivered compared to its advertised features and benefits. This gap between what was promised and what was actually provided was not just disappointing, but also raised concerns about the overall authenticity and value of the app. The user experience did not align with the expectations set by the app’s marketing, leading to a frustrating and unsatisfying experience.

Additionally, when I reached out to The Lasting Change’s customer service for a refund due to these discrepancies, their response was less than accommodating. The lack of flexibility and understanding in addressing my concerns as a customer only compounded my dissatisfaction.

While the physical product (a book) associated with this purchase was of decent quality, it did not make up for the shortcomings of the app and the overall customer service experience.

To potential customers: please be cautious and consider this feedback before deciding to invest in this app. The difference between what is marketed and what you actually receive might be substantial.
